Subject: Discovery Recap & PoC Plan — Oakridge Retail (integration & onboarding)

Hi Asha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed PoC plan so we can align on scope and owners. Please reply if anything looks off or missing.

Key pain points you called out:
- High per-request cost and unpredictable spend around peak traffic (holiday promotions).
- Latency spikes during concurrent catalog re-rating (affects conversion).
- Data residency and PII handling requirements for user messages and receipts.
- Limited visibility into token-level costs and model performance per route.

Current stack you described:
- Backend: Python microservices on AWS ECS (Fargate)
- Frontend: Next.js (TypeScript)
- Existing model usage: OpenAI hosted endpoints for chat + embeddings
- Auth & infra: Internal API gateway + AWS KMS for keys

Success criteria for PoC (what success looks like):
1) Integrate Redwood SDK into the Python rating service and demonstrate 95th percentile latency < 300ms for typical chat flows under baseline traffic.
2) Show >= 30% reduction in token costs vs current baseline via batching/caching and a quantized model route.
3) Validate data controls: configurable retention, audit logs, and optional Private deployment compatibility.

Proposed PoC scope & milestones (4-week plan):
- Week 0 (Kickoff): Access, API keys, add Redwood SDK repo link, define test prompts
- Week 1 (Integration spike): Instrument Python service with SDK + sample calls (Python + Node examples if needed)
- Week 2 (Bench & tune): Load tests, batching config, KV/prefix cache validation
- Week 3 (Quality evals): Run evaluation prompts, compare outputs, adjust model variant/temperature
- Week 4 (Wrap & decision): Final perf/cost report and next-step recommendation

Owners:
- Oakridge: Asha Patel (PM), Tom Reynolds (Platform Lead)
- Redwood: Ben Carter (Account Exec), Marissa Cole (Solutions Engineer)

Integration specifics we discussed:
- SDK languages: primary spike with Python; provide TypeScript examples for frontend maintenance jobs.
- API compatibility: Redwood provides a REST/SDK interface; can mirror your current request/response shape to minimize changes.
- Auth: API keys for hosted; support for mTLS/VPC private peering for Private deployments.

Attachments: oakridge-poc-milestones.xlsx (milestones + acceptance criteria).

Next steps:
1) Asha/Tom: confirm PoC owners and any additional constraints (data residency, legal security checklist).
2) Ben/Marissa: schedule kickoff call (30–45m) and share integration checklist + sample code.

Proposed kickoff: Tue Jul 21, 10:00 AM PT — please confirm availability.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,

Hi Asha / Tom —

Thanks — answering your questions and adding some technical detail so the kickoff can be efficient.

1) Data retention / PII
- Hosted API: configurable retention windows down to 0 days for customer data (we persist request logs for diagnostics; retention configurable per API key/environment).
- Private deployment: full customer control over retention & audit logs (fits strict PII/regulatory controls).
- We also offer automated PII redaction helpers (client-side best practice + server helpers).

2) Quantized model route
- We typically recommend an open quantized model (e.g., Llama2-variants in a quantized flavor) for cost-sensitive routes. That can run on Redwood hosted with curated profiles — no Private deployment required for the PoC. If you need full air-gapped control, Private is an option but not required for initial PoC.

3) SLA / Dedicated options
- Dedicated reserved capacity includes a 99.9% uptime SLA and predictable throughput targets (details in the attached one-pager). For PoC we usually start on hosted and map out Dedicated when you need committed throughput.

Integration checklist (attached: sample-integration-checklist.pdf) — highlights:
- API key provisioning & scoped environments
- Add Redwood Python SDK (pip package) to rating service, small wrapper to match current payloads
- Batching config: start with 50ms latency budget to allow batching without user-visible delay
- KV/prefix cache: identify top-10 prompt prefixes for cache hits
- Telemetry: add token-level cost metrics and per-route latency histogram

Estimated infra footprint for PoC (approx):
- 1x g4dn-like GPU for perf benching (short-lived) or Redwood-hosted benching if you prefer zero infra changes
- No change to production infra during PoC — integration in staging with traffic replay is recommended

Proposed owners and tasks for Week 0/1:
- Asha: provide test prompts + staging access (deadline: Tue Jul 20 COB)
- Tom: provision service account & KMS scope for PoC (deadline: Tue Jul 20 COB)
- Marissa: provide SDK examples and run initial smoke tests (I will drop a small repo link before kickoff)
- Ben: coordinate schedule and success criteria sign-off

Links: PoC plan doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4d-oakridge-poc-plan

I'll attach the sample-integration-checklist.pdf and a short one-pager on Dedicated options. Looking forward to the kickoff.
